data.name: Usage
data.value: play setup [--force] One-time setup: points the game's server names at this PC and trusts a local certificate for them. play setup --remove Undoes everything setup changed. play run Sends the game to the community server. Leave it running while you play.

data.name: SettingsMissing
data.value: settings.json not found: {0}. Keep it next to play.exe.

data.name: SettingsKey
data.value: settings.json: set "{0}" (missing or still a placeholder).

data.name: SettingsUrl
data.value: settings.json: "{0}" must be an https address without a query.

data.name: SettingsHost
data.value: settings.json: "{0}" is not a host name.

data.name: TooEarly
data.value: The official servers stay online until {0}. Setting up now would send the game to the community server instead. Run setup again on or after that day (--force switches now anyway).

data.name: SetupPlan
data.value: setup changes three things on this PC and nothing else (game files are never touched): 1. The Windows hosts file ({3}): {0} of the game's server names point to this PC, between two marked lines. 2. Your Windows trust list (your user only): a local certificate authority named "{1}". It can vouch only for those {0} names; its key is deleted as soon as setup ends and is never saved. 3. A certificate for those names. Its key cannot be exported and stays in your Windows profile; the certificate file is in {2}. Undo all of it at any time: play setup --remove The names:

data.name: SetupTrust
data.value: Windows will now ask whether to trust the certificate authority. Choose Yes.

data.name: Elevate
data.value: Windows will now ask for administrator permission to edit the hosts file (a prompt of its own). Choose Yes. Only that edit runs as administrator.

data.name: HostsFailed
data.value: The hosts file was not changed (permission refused, or a security program blocked it). Run the command again to retry; play setup --remove undoes what was done.

data.name: SetupDone
data.value: Done. Next: start 2-run.cmd (or play run) and leave it open, then start the game. The first time, Windows Firewall asks about the game: click Allow.

data.name: Removed
data.value: Removed the hosts block, the certificate authority and the certificate. The game talks to its own servers again.

data.name: RunNoLeaf
data.value: No certificate found. Run setup first.

data.name: RunLeafExpired
data.value: The certificate has expired. Run setup again: it makes a new one.

data.name: RunNoHosts
data.value: Warning: the hosts file has no block from setup (not run, or removed), so the game still talks to its own servers.

data.name: RunPortBusy
data.value: Could not listen on port 80 or 443: {0} Close the program that uses it (another server, or a second copy of this tool) and try again.

data.name: RunStarted
data.value: Sending the game to {0}. Keep this window open while you play; close it or press Ctrl+C to stop.
